body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported direct CAMCraft jobs for 15, 40 and 80 mm stock. The control plotted the correct depths and rough offsets of 0.245, 0.260 and 0.266 mm, respectively. Each job passed FORMALCHECK with setup and option warnings. See #2999 for verification of the selected quality on the loaded work.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

Port onto the ported #2955 is pushed. The head is `4a94c23ce`. It merges cleanly with `main`.

What the port did:
- It merged `9787bf79e` (the ported #2955, with `main`, #2984 and #3537) into the branch. No rebase and no force-push.
- It used the zero-step setup of #2984 as the frame. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.
- The measured table is now in `camcraft_post::agie_setup`. `PunchSetup20` writes the height into `ID_HEIGHT` of the piece and the work, and into `ID_POSPOSZ`. It refuses a thickness that is not in the table.
- The review text names the thickness and its four offsets.
- The corner check uses the measured rough offset of the thickness. All checks of #2984 and #2955 stay.
- A 20 mm job is byte for byte the same as before.

Gate: quick 343 of 343 steps green. Clippy on `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app` is clean. The PR body has the pinning tests and the readings.

Owed by the author: a fresh offline control import of a 15, 40 and 80 mm job. The earlier control plots used the old writer of this branch. The import must show the height on the piece and the work, zero steps, and the measured offsets.

The PR also changes the `camcraft-mcp` skill row. The body has `Process change: yes`.

1. **Class: incomplete control qualification — `docs/decisions/2954-agie-stock-heights.md:7` and `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md:38`.** Complete the acceptance checks for the current writer. Then confirm the effective quality, measured offsets, retained side, entry and separation with FORMALCHECK and GRAFICHECK. Record the results for every case on this PR. These values are wrong for 40 and 80 mm stock. Make every offset instruction use the table row for the selected stock height. Keep the verification steps consistent with that table and the exported review text.

## Offline control import: punch at 15, 40 and 80 mm (2026-11-23)

The jobs came from head `30e6c4c3f` (the port stack #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969). This head contains the head `4a94c23ce` of this PR.

### Jobs

`examples/agie/punch.camscript` (the 40 × 20 mm rectangle) with these changes only:
- the mesh Z top, the stock `dz`, the WCS origin Z and `top_z` set to 15, 40 or 80;
- the output names `PUNCH15`, `PUNCH40` and `PUNCH80`.

Each receipt says `"working_steps_generated": false`. The review text names the thickness and the offsets of `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`. The SBL files differ from each other only in lines 3, 15 and 44: `ID_HEIGHT` of the piece, `ID_POSPOSZ` and `ID_HEIGHT` of the work.

### Procedure

- Emulated AGIEVISION CUT Classic S. A throwaway clone of the saved state `practice-color-ready`, reloaded before each job.
- Import of the ISO, then the SBL with its SBR, from a read-only floppy image. A host-side read of the guest disk confirmed the imported bytes.
- New piece from `Script Files`. FORMALCHECK with and without warnings. TECCUT assignment. GRAFICHECK. The plot file `1.J00` was copied out and read.

### Readings

| Reading | 15 mm | 40 mm | 80 mm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Tec hoogte` of the work | 15.000 | 40.000 | 80.000 |
| Work line after import | `CCB030[0]` | `CCB030[0]` | `CCB030[0]` |
| FORMALCHECK before TECCUT | `Technologie : te definiëren` only | the same | the same |
| TECCUT header | `Dia:0.25 H:15 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5` | `Dia:0.25 H:40 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5` | `Dia:0.25 H:80 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5` |
| Technology | `estbca25nnn060b030020` | `estbca25nnn060b030050` | `estbca25nnn080b030070` |
| Pre-selected row | `0253 01.36 4`, H column 20 | `0241 00.68 4`, H column 50 | `0235 00.53 4`, H column 70 |
| Work line after TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` | `CCB030[4]` | `CCB030[4]` |
| Pass offsets in the control (µm) | 245, 155, 140, 134 | 260, 170, 140, 130 | 266, 176, 143, 133 |
| `QN2_OFFSETS_UM` (µm) | 245, 155, 140, 134 | 260, 170, 140, 130 | 266, 176, 143, 133 |
| FORMALCHECK after TECCUT | `geen fouten` | `geen fouten` | `geen fouten` |
| Warnings after TECCUT | `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` | the same | the same |

The TECCUT header agrees with each receipt: Berco Cut 0.25, the stock thickness, CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.00 and Te 1.50. At 15 mm the control pre-selects the same technology as at 20 mm. This agrees with the 15 mm row of the table, which has the 20 mm offsets.

### Plot (`1.J00`)

For each thickness:
- Start hole X-30 Y0. Entry at X-20 Y0 on the left face.
- The four faces at the pass offset. Example at 80 mm: X-20.266, Y-10.266, X20.266 and Y10.266 for Main, then 0.176, 0.143 and 0.133 mm for the trims.
- The main loop stops at Y1.000 on the left face and leaves a 1.000 mm separation.
- Each pass returns to X-30 Y0. The separation section then cuts the 1 mm with Main and the three trims.

### Result

All three thicknesses agree with the expectation: the height on the piece and the work, zero steps at import, and the offsets of `QN2_OFFSETS_UM` after TECCUT. I found no mismatch.

### Not checked

- No physical cut.
- The piece height on the control screen was not read separately. The imported SBL bytes (`ID_HEIGHT` of the piece) were checked on the guest disk, and the TECCUT header shows the height.
- Screenshots and the `.J00` files are in the local notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/PUNCH15`, `PUNCH40` and `PUNCH80`.

This PR goes back to draft for one documentation fix. The review of #2968 found it, and the line comes from this PR. In docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md, the TECCUT step gave the 20 mm offsets for every supported thickness. The step now points to the row of the selected thickness in the offsets table. The control readings of 2026-11-23 (my earlier comment) agree with that table at 15, 40 and 80 mm. No code changes. I will push and flag the PR ready again.

Reply to the [review of `4a94c23ce`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2964#issuecomment-7111390385). New head: `3a29a5f9d`.

1. **Incomplete control qualification.** Fresh offline imports from the ported writer ran on 2026-11-23:
   - 15, 40 and 80 mm stock: [results on this PR](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2964#issuecomment-7115464562).
   - `POLY20` and `SLOPE20`: [results on #2955](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2955#issuecomment-7115464026).
   The PR body links both records in "Control check and not exercised".
2. **Fixed height instructions.** Commit `92ca17909` changes step 3 of `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`. The step now points to the row of the selected stock thickness in the QN2 offsets table, in the order rough, trim 1, trim 2, trim 3. It says that the post review names the same four offsets. The 20 mm values stay only as an example.

The new head also merges `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219). The one conflict is in `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`: the resolution keeps the inspection modules of `main` and the QN2 table of this PR. The files under `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/` did not change, and `agie_safe_setup` and `agie_native` pass. Thus the posted bytes of each job are the same as at `92ca17909`. The PR body has the gate readings. The two red quick-gate steps are not in code of this PR (#3774 on `main`, and a 60 s limit under load that passes by name).

Ready for a re-check.
